summary: Inconsistent short-lived STS token rotation between GCP Workload Identity and AWS assume-role sessions causing intermittent access failures
description: Issue summary: Short-lived access failures observed for internal provisioning jobs that use GCP Workload Identity Federation (WIF) to obtain short-lived credentials, then exchange those for AWS STS assume-role sessions. Impact: Several job runs in prod fail with AccessDenied or AssumeRoleTokenExpired errors, causing automated onboarding and dedicated provisioning to stall for ~2-5 minutes before retries succeed. Environment: Production provisioning pipeline (provisioner-v2) operating across us-east GCP project -> us-east-1 AWS accounts. Observed behavior: In the last 72 hours, ~8% of provisioner runs returned errors citing token expiration or invalid audience immediately after successful WIF exchange. Expected behavior: WIF exchange -> STS assume-role should yield a valid AWS session whose lifetime matches the configured duration and not expire immediately. This ticket covers investigation into whether token rotation and session duration values are being propagated consistently across the broker and whether any truncation or mismatch is causing early expiry.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Trigger the provisioning job in prod (provisioner-v2) which uses service-agent@redwood-prod.gserviceaccount to perform WIF exchange.
2) Observe logs from the WIF broker service when it requests an AWS STS token (sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity).
3) Re-run job repeatedly to surface intermittent failures; compare returned Expiration fields from the STS response with job-side token validation immediately after exchange.
4) Inspect Cloud Audit Logs for iam.credentials and AWS CloudTrail for AssumeRole/AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity events for matching request IDs.
5) If failure occurs, capture HTTP body and headers between the broker and AWS STS for analysis (include x-amz-date, x-amz-security-token, and any signed headers).
logs: Sample failures observed (UTC): 2026-03-09T18:22:11Z provisioner: AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity failed: ExpiredToken: Token is expired; status_code=403; WIF exchange trace https://console.cloud.google.com/logs/query; AWS CloudTrail requestId: 3a1b-...-9f2. Notable: STS response 'Expiration' field sometimes equals request time + 1s or shows a timestamp ~5s earlier than current time. Also saw 'InvalidIdentityToken: Audience mismatch' in 2 occurrences.
investigation_notes: Hypotheses: 1) Clock skew between the WIF broker container and AWS validation causing early expiry check. 2) STS session_duration being truncated by an intermediary or defaults overriding requested duration. 3) Tag/session-policy header truncation leading AWS to issue a shorter session. 4) Race where broker reuses an almost-expired token from cache. Actions taken: - Verified NTP status on provisioner pods and WIF broker; found one broker replica with skew ~7s behind; patched daemonset to restart and re-sync via chrony. - Instrumented broker to log requested 'durationSeconds' and STS response 'Expiration' for each exchange (PR in provisioner repo: related_github_prs[0]). - Reviewed infra config: default STS MaxSessionDuration for role ro-provisioner-admin set to 3600s, but broker sometimes requests 43200s; AWS silently reduces to allowed maximum; not root cause for 1s/5s expiry observations. - Found evidence of header truncation on long request URLs in a Go http client wrapper (internal/provisioner/http.go) where 'X-Session-Tags' header was truncated to 256 chars, potentially causing session policy changes. - Added temporary strict cache bypass to broker to rule out reuse of near-expiry tokens. - Correlated incident with deployment of provisioner-v2 2026-03-09T17:40 which updated HTTP client; rollback to previous client eliminated new failures in limited canary. Next steps: Add e2e test for header length, harden client to use chunked metadata, add monitoring alert on any STS response where Expiration < now + 30s.

Infra Engineer - Priya Nair (2026-03-11): Found the HTTP client wrapper truncates long custom headers; opened PR to switch to io.Copy for header propagation (github.com/redwood-inference/provisioner/pull/982).
Marco Li (2026-03-11): Rolled back provisioner-v2 client change in canary; error rate dropped from 8% -> 0.5% over 2 hours. Retaining rollback while we harden client and add tests.

resolution: Partial mitigation applied: rolled back the offending HTTP client change in provisioner-v2 and restarted broker replicas to clear NTP drift and token cache. Implemented a temporary check to reject any STS response where Expiration < now + 30s and trigger immediate retry. Follow-ups required: merge PR to fix header truncation (provisioner PR #982), add e2e test that validates header lengths and STS Expiration sanity, implement pod readiness check for NTP sync, and consider unified token broker that normalizes requested durations. Targeted owner: Marco Li (auth/infra).
